title: 08/03 — Redaction transforms (named procedures with no default in P7)
owner: P7 (injected). The gate's only content operations are resolution and redaction; these are the redaction half. P7 ships no default transform — a redacted_identifier item with a class whose transform is not injected is a load error, never a passthrough.
consumer: the gate's redaction step, at release time, on the materialised excerpt: for each redacted_identifier item the gate resolves (observation_key, span), applies the class's transform to the span, and records the class and outcome in redaction_manifest. Catalogue 02 names which transform each class uses.

design_anchor.quote: The gate never truncates and never reduces

rules_preamble: **Redaction removes a value; it never rewrites a document.** Reduction — summarizing, shortening, choosing what the model sees — is a dossier decision and a dossier decision is P8's, made BEFORE the gate is called. The gate's transforms operate on single spans and nothing else.

**Context always survives.** P4 publishes context_before / context_after / context_truncated as three fields precisely "so that §8.4 can redact a value without dropping its context" (P5 SPEC, M5). Every transform below leaves both context fields byte-identical; a transform that touches context is malformed by definition.

**Every transform is locally reversible in the only sense 00 permits:** the original value remains in local SQLite (the always-local set includes complete extracted text and raw sensitive values) and the dossier carries the redacted form. Nothing is reversible FROM the dossier — that would defeat redaction; reversibility means the local record can always reconstruct exactly what left, which is the audit record's stated obligation.

**No transform may manufacture a join key.** Hashing or pseudonymizing a value would let two dossiers be joined on the same person across files; 00 nowhere allows it, so it is forbidden (see refused).
**No numbers.** keep_last_n's n is an injected slot with no default; nothing in this file carries a numeric value.

injected_slots.meaning: how many trailing characters keep_last_n retains; per-class override permitted at the injection site

entries.name: Replace span with a class token
entries.input: the materialised excerpt text, one (start, end) span within it, and the identifier class_id
entries.output: the excerpt with the span replaced by the literal token '[' + class_id + ']' — e.g. [government_id_number]; span length is deliberately not preserved
preserves: every byte of the excerpt outside the span
the fact THAT a value of this class stood here — the token says so
never_does: vary the token per value (a per-value token would be a pseudonym and joinable)
leak span length by padding the token

design_cites.quote: selected excerpts, redacted identifiers, candidate labels, non-sensitive metadata, and evidence references

entries.notes: the default-shaped transform for most classes: the model learns a value of this KIND was present, which is often exactly the evidence a dossier question needs ('is this an account statement?'), while the value itself stays local

entries.name: Class token plus retained tail
entries.input: the materialised excerpt text, one span, the identifier class_id, and the injected redaction_keep_n
entries.output: the span replaced by '[' + class_id + ' …' + the span's final redaction_keep_n characters + ']' — e.g. [financial_account_number …6819]
preserves: the trailing characters statement conventions already display
never_does: retain more than redaction_keep_n characters, or derive the count from the value's length
retain a LEADING prefix (prefixes carry issuer/type information trailing digits do not)
apply to any class marked always_local — a dropping transform is mandatory there
truncate, summarize, or touch text outside the span
entries.notes: exists because a tail is sometimes the discriminating evidence — 'which of the two accounts is this statement for?' is answerable from the tail without the locator; the audit record's per-item manifest still marks the value redacted

entries.name: Remove span entirely
entries.input: the materialised excerpt text, one span, and the identifier class_id
entries.output: the excerpt with the span removed and nothing inserted; the redaction_manifest entry — not the text — records that a value of this class was dropped
never_does: leave any fragment of the value, of any length
insert a marker that names the class in the text (for always-local material even the class's presence-in-text is withheld; the manifest, which stays in the audit record, is the honest ledger)
drop more than the span — the surrounding sentence survives

design_cites.quote: Paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, user edits, group memberships, and raw sensitive values should remain local.

entries.notes: the transform for always_local classes (authentication_secret): the dossier reads as if the value were never there, the audit record knows it was, and the section-8.6 rule against silent truncation is honored because the DECISIVE evidence for any legitimate dossier question is never a secret's value — a dossier whose question requires the secret itself is a request the gate should be denying, not redacting

entries.name: Remove GPS coordinate pair
entries.input: the materialised excerpt text and one span covering a coordinate pair (or a metadata_field resolution that turned out to carry coordinates)
entries.output: the excerpt with the coordinate pair removed and nothing inserted; for a metadata_field item that resolves to coordinates the item is emptied and the manifest records the drop
preserves: non-location neighbouring metadata (a capture YEAR may still travel as its own non-sensitive metadata_field — the year is a Photos fact, the coordinates are not)
never_does: coarsen, round, or generalize coordinates to a city or region — a generalized location is an invented value, and inventing values is the extractors' cardinal sin as much as the gate's
substitute a place NAME resolved from the coordinates — that is derivation, which moves information the always-local rule says stays home
leave one coordinate of the pair

design_cites.quote: Paths, complete extracted text, OCR output, file hashes, image EXIF, GPS, user edits, group memberships, and raw sensitive values should remain local.

entries.notes: GPS is always-local by name; this transform exists for coordinates that surface INSIDE releasable text (maps-screenshot OCR, captions). The gate's item-kind rules already refuse EXIF/GPS as metadata items; drop_gps is the backstop for text-embedded coordinates

refused.refuses: any model-assisted 'smart' redaction, paraphrase, or privacy-preserving rewrite
refused.why: reduction changes what the model sees, which is a dossier decision — P8's, before the gate. The gate's own contract states "The gate never truncates and never reduces" (P7 SPEC); a rewriting transform would also require a model call to sanitize input TO a model call, which is circular.

design_cites.quote: The gate never truncates and never reduces

refused.refuses: hashing or tokenizing a value into a stable per-value pseudonym
refused.why: a stable pseudonym is a join key: the same person's identifier hashes identically across files and dossiers, so an external provider could correlate what redaction exists to keep uncorrelatable. 00 never allows it; the dispatch names it a never_does and it is promoted here to a refused transform.

refused.refuses: generalizing transforms (coordinates to city, birth date to age band, account to institution)
refused.why: every generalization manufactures a value nobody observed; the product's evidence discipline forbids invented values everywhere else and the gate is not an exception. Where the general fact is legitimately needed, it already exists as a FACT (institution, capture year) and travels as candidate_label or metadata_field.

refused.refuses: masking that preserves length and format (X99-XX-9999 shapes)
refused.why: format-preserving output leaks the value's shape and length, which for short identifier spaces is real information; the class token already conveys the kind without the shape.

uncertain.question: A document may itself contain literal text shaped like a class token ('[government_id_number]' in a privacy-policy PDF). The manifest disambiguates for the audit trail, but the MODEL cannot distinguish source text from redaction.
uncertain.both_sides: Escaping source-text brackets alters bytes outside the span (forbidden); accepting the ambiguity costs nothing measurable. Recorded so the choice is deliberate.

uncertain.question: Two identifier spans can overlap (an account number inside a longer quoted string that is itself a secret). Apply order matters for manifest bookkeeping.
uncertain.both_sides: Widest-span-first with inner spans recorded as subsumed is the obvious rule; stating it here would be inventing gate mechanics, which are P7's build. Flagged for the implementer.
